description:
Found by defk-ds0 (examples/release_debian on branch defk-ds0/debian-release). Defk.Build writes each kernel .so to _build/<env>/defk/ and the generated __defk_load__ loads it from that absolute build path. mix release does not copy that directory, so a release boots with on_load_function_failed (cannot open shared object file) and the module is undefined. The ds0 Dockerfile works around it by copying _build/prod/defk to the same absolute path in the runtime image.

Fix: write the .so under the owning app's priv/ (as elixir_make packages do) and load it via :code.priv_dir/1 (or Application.app_dir) at load time, so it travels with the release and survives relocation. Keep the content-hash cache behaviour.

Done when the ds0 Dockerfile builds and runs with COPY_SO=0 (no manual copy), a test checks the load path is relative to the app's priv dir, and examples/release_debian/README.md drops the workaround.
title: Ship kernel .so files in mix releases
